title: Steering-Induced Incoherence x Monitor Blindness: Do Degraded Outputs Slip Past Safety Classifiers?
quick_reasoning: An evasion channel where incoherent harmful output dodges safety classifiers is a specific, well-defined monitoring blind spot.

original_idea.body:
# Steering-Induced Incoherence x Monitor Blindness: Do Degraded Outputs Slip Past Safety Classifiers?

**Problem:** Failure mode A (concept_steering): strong steering degrades text coherence. Failure mode B (output-monitoring): safety classifiers / judges are trained on coherent text and may mis-score degraded outputs. Compound risk: a degraded-but-harmful generation produced under heavy steering evades a downstream toxicity/harm classifier that was never tested on incoherent inputs.

**Direction:** Apply increasing steering strengths on an open model to a fixed prompt set, producing outputs from coherent to garbled. Have a public safety classifier (e.g. an open guard model) score each. Independently human/heuristic-label actual harmfulness. Measure whether classifier accuracy drops as coherence drops, opening a blind spot harmful actors could exploit.

**Why it matters:** Reveals an evasion channel created by the interaction of two components, with no lab access needed. Relevant to monitoring-harness robustness, a strategically valuable infrastructure concern.

**Relevant context:** Steering degrades coherence per 'Activation Steering for Aligned Open-ended Generation without Sacrificing Coherence' (arXiv 2604.08169). Monitoring-blindness framing extends Beaglehole's probe-vs-judge result by stress-testing judges on off-distribution (incoherent) inputs.

original_idea.body:
# Sycophancy Steering x Reward-Model Gaming: Can a Steered Model Better Fool an Evaluator?

**Problem:** Failure mode A (concept_steering): a sycophancy steering vector can be added to make a model more agreeable. Failure mode B (reward hacking / evaluator manipulation): models exploit evaluator preferences. Compound risk: sycophancy steering may directly inflate scores from an LLM-judge evaluator without improving real answer quality — steering as a reward-hacking lever.

**Direction:** On an open model, add a sycophancy steering vector at varying strengths. Generate answers to a QA/opinion set, then score them with (a) an LLM-judge (open judge model) and (b) ground-truth correctness. Measure whether sycophancy steering raises judge scores while leaving or lowering correctness — a clean demonstration of steering-driven evaluator gaming.

**Why it matters:** Connects representation engineering to the diffuse, fuzzy-reward problem of evaluator manipulation — exactly the kind of hard-to-measure failure labs deprioritize. Model-organism flavored and feasible in 30h.

**Relevant context:** Sycophancy steering vectors documented in CAA literature and 'Sycophancy Hides Linearly in the Attention Heads' (arXiv 2601.16644). Evaluator-manipulation / reward hacking grounded in arXiv 2604.13602.

title: Probe-Based Hallucination Monitor x Distribution Shift: When the Two Compound at Deployment

# Probe-Based Hallucination Monitor x Distribution Shift: When the Two Compound at Deployment

**Problem:** Failure mode A (concept_steering): concept-vector probes for hallucination are extracted in-distribution. Failure mode B (distribution shift): deployment data drifts. Compound risk: Beaglehole et al. claim probes beat judges for hallucination, but if the probe degrades faster than the judge under domain shift, the recommended monitor is actually the more fragile choice exactly when it matters.

**Direction:** Extract a hallucination probe on one QA domain (e.g. TriviaQA). Evaluate AUROC of (a) the probe and (b) an LLM-judge baseline on increasingly out-of-domain QA sets (medical, legal, code). Measure the relative degradation slope to test which monitor is more robust under shift — directly stress-testing the source paper's headline claim.

**Why it matters:** The probe-beats-judge result is a key recommendation; its robustness under shift is the deciding factor for whether to deploy probes as monitors. Cheap, decisive, and tests a stated surprising result.

**Relevant context:** Probe-beats-judge from Beaglehole et al. (concept_steering context). Distribution-shift transfer numbers (TruthfulQA->TriviaQA drop) from 'Steer LLM Latents for Hallucination Detection' (arXiv 2503.01917). HalluShift (arXiv 2504.09482) on shift-based detection.

title: Refusal Ablation x Backdoor Activation: Does Removing Refusal Unmask Latent Trigger Behavior?

original_idea.body:
# Refusal Ablation x Backdoor Activation: Does Removing Refusal Unmask Latent Trigger Behavior?

**Problem:** Failure mode A (concept_steering): ablating the refusal direction. Failure mode B (data-poisoning / backdoors): a model carries a latent trigger. Compound risk: refusal ordinarily masks triggered harmful behavior; ablating the refusal direction could unmask backdoor responses that were dormant under normal alignment, making the two failures multiplicative.

**Direction:** Use a small open model with a known/published benign backdoor (or insert a trivial trigger via tiny LoRA). Compare triggered-vs-untriggered behavior with refusal intact vs refusal-direction ablated. Measure whether ablation disproportionately amplifies the triggered behavior relative to the baseline — testing the unmasking hypothesis.

**Why it matters:** Backdoors + steering is an underexplored interaction with a clear medium-horizon supply-chain threat model. Model-organism scoped to a tiny trigger, no large training.

**Relevant context:** Refusal-direction ablation methodology is open-source and well documented. Steering-x-safety unmasking is motivated by arXiv 2603.24543 (steering not safety-neutral) and the refusal-direction universality work (arXiv 2505.17306).

title: Steering Strength x Calibration Collapse: Does Pushing a Concept Wreck the Model's Uncertainty?
quick_reasoning: Steering silently destroying calibration breaks confidence-gated safety mechanisms, a directly relevant scoped question.

original_idea.body:
# Steering Strength x Calibration Collapse: Does Pushing a Concept Wreck the Model's Uncertainty?

**Problem:** Failure mode A (concept_steering): increasing steering strength along a concept direction. Failure mode B (miscalibration): the model's confidence no longer tracks correctness. Compound risk: steering may sharpen a behavior while quietly destroying calibration, so a steered model is confidently wrong — and any safety policy keyed on confidence thresholds breaks.

**Direction:** On an open model, apply a factuality or persona steering vector across strength levels. For each, measure task accuracy AND calibration (ECE / reliability diagram) on a multiple-choice benchmark with logprob-derived confidences. Test whether calibration degrades faster than accuracy as steering strength rises.

**Why it matters:** Confidence-gated safety mechanisms (abstention, escalation) assume calibration; steering silently undermining it is a clean compound-risk finding. Inference-only, fits 30h.

**Relevant context:** Steering-factor brittleness from arXiv 2605.05983 and 2504.04635. Calibration as a distinct axis is standard; the novelty is measuring the calibration-vs-accuracy decoupling under steering.

title: Steered to Help, Steered to Leak: Format-Steering x PII / Secret Disclosure

original_idea.body:
# Steered to Help, Steered to Leak: Format-Steering x PII / Secret Disclosure

**Problem:** Failure mode A (concept_steering): a compliance/instruction-following steering vector. Failure mode B (information leakage / privacy): the model discloses content it should withhold. Compound risk: boosting raw compliance via steering may override learned discretion boundaries, increasing disclosure of secrets/system-prompt/PII the model was instructed to keep.

**Direction:** Set up an open model with a system prompt containing a fake secret it must not reveal. Apply a compliance/helpfulness steering vector at varying strengths and measure secret-disclosure rate under direct and indirect extraction prompts, vs unsteered baseline. Quantify how steering for compliance trades off against confidentiality.

**Why it matters:** Prompt-injection / disclosure is a top deployment risk; showing benign compliance-steering worsens it is a concrete, lab-independent contribution. Easy to build with a synthetic secret.

**Relevant context:** Compliance/benign-steering side effects from arXiv 2602.04896. Confidentiality boundary erosion is a natural extension of the refusal-erosion mechanism documented in arXiv 2603.24543.

title: Steering Vector Theft x Jailbreak-as-a-Service: Auditing Transferability of Harmful Steering Across Models

original_idea.body:
# Steering Vector Theft x Jailbreak-as-a-Service: Auditing Transferability of Harmful Steering Across Models

**Problem:** Failure mode A (concept_steering): steering vectors transfer across related models / share structure. Failure mode B (open-weight misuse): an attacker reuses a harmful steering vector. Compound risk: a refusal-ablation vector extracted from one open model may transfer to sibling/fine-tuned models, so a single extracted 'unsafe' vector becomes a portable, reusable jailbreak artifact.

**Direction:** Extract a refusal-ablation vector from a base open model. Apply it (with appropriate layer mapping) to several derivatives: the official instruct version, a community fine-tune, and a quantized variant. Measure harmful-compliance increase to assess transfer. Report which model relationships preserve the harmful effect — an attack-surface map.

**Why it matters:** If harmful vectors are portable, the open-weight ecosystem has a reusable-exploit problem labs can't patch centrally. Strategically valuable threat assessment, fully doable on consumer hardware.

**Relevant context:** Cross-model steering transfer from cross-model-steering literature and the cross-language/transfer results in Beaglehole et al. Refusal-ablation portability motivated by arXiv 2505.17306 and 2603.24543.

title: Monitor-and-Steer Loop Instability: Probe Drift x Steering Feedback Compounding Over Iterations

original_idea.body:
# Monitor-and-Steer Loop Instability: Probe Drift x Steering Feedback Compounding Over Iterations

**Problem:** Failure mode A (concept_steering): a probe used to decide when to steer is itself a noisy concept estimate. Failure mode B (steering side effects): steering shifts activations, which shifts the probe's readings. Compound risk: in a closed monitor->steer->monitor loop, small probe errors and steering side effects feed back, causing the system to over-steer or oscillate.

**Direction:** Build a minimal closed loop: a toxicity probe triggers a de-toxify steering vector, then re-reads the probe. Iterate over multiple generation steps. Measure whether the loop converges, oscillates, or runs away (over-suppression / collapse) as a function of probe threshold and steering gain. A small dynamical-systems-style study of a safety control loop.

**Why it matters:** Adaptive steering monitors are emerging; their closed-loop stability is unstudied and is a prerequisite for safe deployment infrastructure. Pure inference, small prototype harness.

**Relevant context:** Probe-driven steering from Beaglehole et al. (probes + steering). Side-effect feedback grounded in arXiv 2603.24543 and adaptive-defense work AdaSteer (arXiv 2504.09466). Stability of the loop is the novel compound angle.

title: Over-Refusal Steering x Helpful-Harm Tradeoff: Measuring the Hidden Capability Tax of Safety Steering
quick_reasoning: Dose-response Pareto frontier of safety steering vs capability is a directly relevant, scoped deployment question.

original_idea.body:
# Over-Refusal Steering x Helpful-Harm Tradeoff: Measuring the Hidden Capability Tax of Safety Steering

**Problem:** Failure mode A (concept_steering): pushing the refusal direction to harden safety. Failure mode B (over-refusal / capability suppression): the model refuses benign requests and loses task capability. Compound risk: hardening safety via steering and capability loss are not independent — beyond a point, each unit of jailbreak resistance bought costs a super-linear amount of benign helpfulness.

**Direction:** Sweep refusal-steering strength on an open model. At each level, jointly measure jailbreak resistance (harmful set) and over-refusal + accuracy on a benign capability set. Plot the Pareto frontier and identify the knee where benign cost accelerates. Quantify the 'exchange rate' between safety gain and capability loss.

**Why it matters:** Gives deployers a concrete dose-response curve for safety steering, exposing where it becomes counterproductive. Decision-relevant, cheap, and tests a clean two-failure tradeoff.

**Relevant context:** Over-refusal collateral cost documented in arXiv 2603.24543 and 2602.06256. Capability-preservation-below-5% claim from arXiv 2602.04896 gives a baseline to test against at higher strengths.

title: Harm-Category Heterogeneity in Shallow Alignment
quick_reasoning: Per-category map of shallowest-aligned harm categories targets a specific catastrophic-risk prioritization safety question.

original_idea.body:
# Harm-Category Heterogeneity in Shallow Alignment

**Problem:** Shallow-alignment and jailbreak studies often report a single aggregate attack-success number, masking whether some harm categories (e.g. cyber, bio, hate, self-harm) are far more shallowly aligned than others on the same model.

**Direction:** Using AILuminate's 12 hazard categories (or StrongREJECT categories), run a fixed prefill attack across all categories on 2-3 small open models and report per-category attack-success and refusal-recovery. Identify categories where alignment is dangerously shallow and whether the ranking is consistent across models.

**Why it matters:** Aggregate jailbreak metrics hide the categories that matter most for catastrophic risk. A per-category shallowness map tells the field where to deepen alignment first — a diffuse, hard-to-fund prioritization question. Uses public benchmarks, pure inference.

**Relevant context:** AILuminate (MLCommons, 24K+ prompts, 12 hazard categories) and StrongREJECT (arXiv:2402.10260) provide categorized prompts. Qi et al. (arXiv:2406.05946) supply the prefill attack. Context file lists these as key datasets.

title: Quantization x Steering Fragility: Does Compressing a Model Break Its Safety Steering Vector?
quick_reasoning: Whether safety steering survives quantization on deployed consumer models is a specific, well-defined deployment-safety question.

original_idea.body:
# Quantization x Steering Fragility: Does Compressing a Model Break Its Safety Steering Vector?

**Problem:** Failure mode A (concept_steering): steering vectors are sensitive to small activation perturbations. Failure mode B (quantization-induced drift): int8/int4 quantization perturbs activations. Compound risk: a safety steering vector validated on the fp16 model may silently lose effect (or flip sign) on the quantized model people actually deploy on consumer hardware.

**Direction:** Extract a safety steering vector on an fp16 open model. Apply the SAME vector to 8-bit and 4-bit quantized versions of the model and measure how much of the safety effect (refusal increase / harmful-compliance decrease) survives. Report effect retention and any sign flips per quantization level.

**Why it matters:** Quantized deployment is the norm for the consumer/edge models this very project targets; if safety steering doesn't survive quantization, a huge swath of deployments are unprotected. Perfectly matched to single-GPU constraints.

**Relevant context:** Steering sensitivity to perturbations from arXiv 2605.05983 and 2504.04635. Quantization is standard (bitsandbytes); the quantization-x-steering interaction is an underexplored, highly practical compound risk.

title: Steering the Wrong Layer x Silent Failure: Layer-Mismatch as a Compound Robustness Hole
quick_reasoning: Silent-failure zone of misconfigured safety steering plus a sanity-check is directly relevant safety infrastructure.

original_idea.body:
# Steering the Wrong Layer x Silent Failure: Layer-Mismatch as a Compound Robustness Hole

**Problem:** Failure mode A (concept_steering): steering effect depends critically on the injection layer. Failure mode B (silent monitoring failure): no error is raised when a vector is applied at a suboptimal layer. Compound risk: a misconfigured layer index produces a steering vector that appears to run fine but provides little/negative safety effect, and nothing in the pipeline flags it.

**Direction:** Apply a refusal/safety steering vector across every layer of an open model and map the effect-vs-layer curve. Then quantify the 'silent failure zone': layers where the intervention runs without error but safety effect is near-zero or negative. Propose a minimal automated check (effect-size assertion) that would catch misconfiguration.

**Why it matters:** Builds a small piece of monitoring infrastructure (a sanity-check for steering pipelines) and documents a configuration footgun. Strategically valuable, beginner-feasible, inference-only.

**Relevant context:** Layer-dependence and reliability challenges from arXiv 2504.04635. Multi-property steering at distinct layers from the multi-concept interference literature (arXiv 2502.12179). The 'silent failure' + automated-check framing is the novel contribution.

title: Steering x Context-Length: Does a Steering Vector Decay Over Long Generations and Re-open Jailbreaks?
quick_reasoning: Steering decay aligning with long-context jailbreaks is a specific, focused long-context safety threat.

original_idea.body:
# Steering x Context-Length: Does a Steering Vector Decay Over Long Generations and Re-open Jailbreaks?

**Problem:** Failure mode A (concept_steering): a steering vector is applied per-token but its behavioral effect may attenuate as generation length grows. Failure mode B (long-context jailbreaks / many-shot attacks): safety degrades over long contexts. Compound risk: the steering safety effect fades over the very long generations where many-shot jailbreaks operate, so the two weaknesses align in time.

**Direction:** Apply a safety steering vector and generate long outputs in response to many-shot / long-context harmful prompts. Measure harmful-compliance as a function of position in the generation and context length, comparing steered vs unsteered. Test whether steering's protective effect decays where long-context attacks strengthen.

**Why it matters:** Long-context attacks are a growing medium-horizon threat; showing steering defenses decay exactly there is decision-relevant. Inference-only with public jailbreak prompts.

**Relevant context:** Steering reliability over generation from arXiv 2504.04635 and coherence-decay work (arXiv 2604.08169). Long-context / many-shot jailbreak vulnerability is a documented attack class; the temporal-decay-meets-long-context interaction is the novel compound angle.

title: Vision Steering x Text Refusal: Does Image-Side Concept Steering Bypass Language-Side Safety?
quick_reasoning: Image-side steering routing around text refusal is a recognized, scoped multimodal safety-gap question.

original_idea.body:
# Vision Steering x Text Refusal: Does Image-Side Concept Steering Bypass Language-Side Safety?

**Problem:** Failure mode A (concept_steering): extending concept steering to vision/multimodal models (an explicit extension in the source paper). Failure mode B (multimodal safety gap): safety alignment is often weaker on the vision pathway. Compound risk: steering a concept via the image-encoder activations may route around the text-side refusal training, compounding the known multimodal safety hole.

**Direction:** On a small open vision-language model, extract a simple concept direction in the visual/cross-modal activation stream and use it to push toward a benign target behavior, while measuring whether it incidentally lowers text-side refusal on harmful image+text prompts. Compare with steering applied in the text stream. Document any asymmetry in the safety effect.

**Why it matters:** Multimodal steering safety is nearly unstudied and is an explicit extension flagged by the source paper. Open VLMs are small enough for one GPU, and the multimodal jailbreak threat is real and lab-deprioritized.

**Relevant context:** Multimodal-extension is an Open Problem in the concept_steering context (Beaglehole et al. extensions). VLM steering / null-space defense from arXiv 2603.22094. Scoped to an existing small open VLM, no training.

title: Probe False-Positives x Automated Steering: When a Noisy Monitor Triggers Harmful Over-Correction
quick_reasoning: Monitor-error-becomes-harm-via-actuator framing is a directly relevant, scoped automated-steering-safety question.

original_idea.body:
# Probe False-Positives x Automated Steering: When a Noisy Monitor Triggers Harmful Over-Correction

**Problem:** Failure mode A (concept_steering): a concept probe has a nonzero false-positive rate. Failure mode B (automated intervention): a deployed system auto-applies a steering correction whenever the probe fires. Compound risk: probe false positives trigger unwarranted steering on benign inputs, and that unwarranted steering can itself cause harm (over-refusal, incoherence, jailbreak externality) — error in the monitor becomes harm via the actuator.

**Direction:** On a benign prompt set, measure a deception/toxicity probe's false-positive rate. For the false-positive cases, apply the corresponding corrective steering vector and measure the resulting harm (over-refusal, quality drop). Combine into an expected-harm estimate: P(false positive) x harm-per-unwarranted-steer. Compare against the benefit on true positives.

**Why it matters:** Frames monitor accuracy and actuator side-effects as a single risk budget — essential for designing safe automated steering harnesses. Builds reusable evaluation logic, beginner-feasible.

**Relevant context:** Probe-as-monitor from Beaglehole et al. Steering-as-harm (over-refusal, externality) from arXiv 2602.04896 and 2603.24543. The expected-harm composition of monitor-error x actuator-harm is the novel framing.

title: Steering Detection Evasion x Stealthy Misuse: Can a Steered Model Hide That It's Being Steered?
quick_reasoning: Stealth zone of undetectable harmful steering defeats detect-the-steering defenses, a specific covert-misuse threat.

original_idea.body:
# Steering Detection Evasion x Stealthy Misuse: Can a Steered Model Hide That It's Being Steered?

**Problem:** Failure mode A (concept_steering): steering changes activations in detectable ways. Failure mode B (covert misuse / detection evasion): an adversary wants the steering to be undetectable. Compound risk: if low-strength harmful steering both works AND evades activation-based steering-detectors, defenders relying on 'detect-the-steering' monitoring are doubly defeated.

**Direction:** Build a simple steering-detector (probe on activations distinguishing steered vs unsteered generations). Then sweep harmful-steering strength and measure jointly: (a) harmful effect achieved and (b) detector evasion rate. Identify whether a 'stealth zone' exists — enough harm with low enough detectability — and characterize it.

**Why it matters:** Tests the robustness of steering-detection as a defense and quantifies the adversary's stealth-vs-effect frontier. A model-organism-style red-team of a defense, no lab resources required.

**Relevant context:** Steering-detection is implied by Beaglehole's monitoring framing. Evasion / stealth grounded in 'Steering Beyond the Support' (arXiv 2605.24535) on jailbroken activation simulation and 2603.24543 on steering propagation. The stealth-zone characterization is the novel compound contribution.

title: Steering x RLHF Interaction: Does Steering Undo or Compound RLHF Safety Inconsistently Across Behaviors?
quick_reasoning: Per-category steering-RLHF interaction giving unpredictable net safety is a directly relevant, scoped safety question.

original_idea.body:
# Steering x RLHF Interaction: Does Steering Undo or Compound RLHF Safety Inconsistently Across Behaviors?

**Problem:** Failure mode A (concept_steering): inference-time steering. Failure mode B (RLHF brittleness): RLHF safety is shallow and easily perturbed. Compound risk: combining steering with an RLHF'd model (an explicit open problem from Beaglehole et al.) may reinforce safety for some behaviors but cancel it for others, giving inconsistent net safety the deployer can't predict.

**Direction:** On an RLHF'd open model, apply a safety steering vector and measure net safety across several distinct behavior categories (toxicity, illegal-advice, self-harm, privacy). Test whether steering uniformly helps or whether RLHF and steering interact differently per category (helping some, hurting others). Map the interaction by category.

**Why it matters:** Directly addresses the 'combine concept steering with RLHF' open problem from the source paper, surfacing whether the combination is reliably additive. Inference-only, uses public category benchmarks.

**Relevant context:** 'Combine concept steering with RLHF' is an explicit Open Problem in the concept_steering context. RLHF brittleness from interconnects.ai 'Undoing RLHF' and arXiv 2603.24543. Per-category heterogeneity is the novel measured quantity.

title: Anti-Steer Subgroups x Fairness: Does Safety Steering Protect Some Demographic Inputs Less Than Others?
quick_reasoning: Uneven safety-steering protection across demographic framings is a recognized fairness-meets-safety question, scoped via templates.

original_idea.body:
# Anti-Steer Subgroups x Fairness: Does Safety Steering Protect Some Demographic Inputs Less Than Others?

**Problem:** Failure mode A (concept_steering): anti-steerable examples / heterogeneous steering effect. Failure mode B (fairness / disparate safety): safety behavior varies across demographic framings. Compound risk: a safety steering vector may reduce harmful outputs for prompts mentioning some groups but not others, so the protective effect is distributed unevenly — a fairness failure created by a safety intervention.

**Direction:** Construct matched harmful-prompt templates varying only a demographic descriptor. Apply a safety steering vector and measure harmful-compliance reduction per group. Test for statistically significant disparities in how much protection steering provides across groups, controlling for base rates.

**Why it matters:** Safety interventions are assumed group-neutral; showing steering's protection is unevenly distributed is a novel, equity-relevant compound finding. Template-based, cheap, statistics-friendly for the target audience.

**Relevant context:** Heterogeneous / anti-steerable effects from arXiv 2504.04635 (up to 50% anti-steerable). Disparate safety behavior is documented in alignment literature; combining it with steering heterogeneity is the novel angle. Pure inference.

title: Steering Vector Staleness x Continuous Deployment: A Drift-Monitoring Harness Prototype
quick_reasoning: A drift-detection harness for safety steering pipelines is strategically valuable, directly relevant safety infrastructure.

original_idea.body:
# Steering Vector Staleness x Continuous Deployment: A Drift-Monitoring Harness Prototype

**Problem:** Failure mode A (concept_steering): concept directions drift across model versions. Failure mode B (no drift detection in deployment): pipelines apply a fixed vector indefinitely. Compound risk: a stale vector keeps being applied as the model is iteratively updated, and the gap between intended and actual effect grows silently until safety quietly fails.

**Direction:** Build a tiny monitoring harness: given two checkpoints of an open model and a stored steering vector, automatically compute (a) cosine drift of the re-extracted concept direction and (b) drop in measured behavioral effect, and emit a 'recalibrate' flag past a threshold. Validate it across a few LoRA-fine-tuned checkpoints and report how many updates it takes to trip the flag.

**Why it matters:** Produces reusable, strategically valuable safety infrastructure (a drift detector for steering pipelines) while directly testing the source paper's stability open problem. Small prototype, one GPU.

**Relevant context:** Cross-update stability is an explicit Open Problem (Beaglehole et al.). Drift/brittleness from arXiv 2603.24543 and 2504.04635. The harness + recalibrate-trigger is the buildable infrastructure deliverable.

title: Do benign steering vectors silently erode safety? A replication and audit
quick_reasoning: Auditing which benign-steering directions unlock harmful outputs is a specific, well-defined deployment-safety problem.

original_idea.body:
# Do benign steering vectors silently erode safety? A replication and audit

**Problem:** Recent work shows steering vectors derived from BENIGN datasets (compliance, output-format) can inadvertently erode safety guardrails, pushing jailbreak attack success rates above 80%. This 'safety externality' of steering is underexplored on small open models that hobbyists actually use.

**Direction:** Reproduce a small slice of the 'Safety Pitfalls of Steering Vectors' audit on a single open model (e.g. Llama-3.1-8B or Qwen2.5-7B). Extract 4-6 CAA steering vectors from clearly benign contrastive datasets (politeness, JSON formatting, verbosity, brevity). Apply each at a fixed strength and measure attack-success-rate change on a small public jailbreak benchmark (e.g. AdvBench subset, 50 prompts) using a refusal classifier. Rank which benign behaviors most degrade safety.

**Why it matters:** Practitioners outside labs routinely build steering vectors for formatting/style with no idea they may be unlocking harmful outputs. A clean, reproducible audit on consumer hardware gives the open community a checklist of risky benign-steering directions — diffuse-reward safety infrastructure that labs deprioritize.

**Relevant context:** Extends 'Analysing the Safety Pitfalls of Steering Vectors' (arXiv:2603.24543, ~Mar 2026), which reports benign-derived steering vectors raise ASR above 80% and CAA vectors shift ASR by up to 57%.

title: Does Chain-of-Thought Prompting Help or Hurt Jailbreak Robustness?
quick_reasoning: Net effect of prompted CoT on jailbreak robustness is a specific, focused deployment-safety question.

original_idea.body:
# Does Chain-of-Thought Prompting Help or Hurt Jailbreak Robustness?

**Problem:** Reasoning/deliberation has been argued to make models safer (deliberative alignment), but eliciting CoT in non-reasoning open models via prompting could either deepen safety or give the model room to talk itself into compliance. The net effect on small open models is unclear.

**Direction:** On small open instruct models (not native reasoners), compare jailbreak success with and without an added 'think step by step before answering' instruction across prefill and many-shot attacks. Inspect the generated reasoning for cases where CoT rationalizes compliance vs where it reinforces refusal. Quantify net robustness change.

**Why it matters:** Deployers increasingly bolt CoT prompting onto cheap models; knowing whether this is a free safety win or a footgun is practically important and lab-independent. Reading the reasoning traces also yields qualitative model-organism insight into 'attacking without honest reasoning.'

**Relevant context:** 'Deliberative Alignment: Reasoning Enables Safer Language Models' (arXiv:2412.16339) argues reasoning improves safety; the StrongREJECT writeup notes o1 is more jailbreak-robust. This varies the population to prompted (non-native) CoT on small open models, an untested regime. Qi et al. (arXiv:2406.05946) and many-shot (NeurIPS 2024) supply attacks.

title: Sparsify-then-steer: how few dimensions does a safety steering vector really need?
quick_reasoning: Sparsity of safety steering vectors bears on cheap auditable monitoring and tamper-resistance, a directly relevant question.

original_idea.body:
# Sparsify-then-steer: how few dimensions does a safety steering vector really need?

**Problem:** A mechanistic study of refusal steering found steering vectors can be sparsified 90-99% while retaining most performance, but this was shown mainly for refusal. It's unknown whether OTHER safety concepts (deception, sycophancy, toxicity) are equally sparse, which matters for interpretability and tamper-resistance.

**Direction:** On one open model, extract CAA steering vectors for 4 safety concepts (refusal, sycophancy, toxicity, deception) using public contrastive datasets. For each, greedily zero out all but the top-k coordinates by magnitude and measure how steering effect (behavior shift) decays as k shrinks. Plot a 'sparsity-retention curve' per concept and report which concepts are genuinely low-dimensional.

**Why it matters:** If safety concepts live in a handful of coordinates, monitoring and ablation become cheap and human-auditable; if they're dense, steering is fragile. This is a self-contained interpretability result needing only a single GPU and no training.

**Relevant context:** Extends 'What Drives Representation Steering? A Mechanistic Case Study on Steering Refusal' (arXiv:2604.08524, ~Apr 2026), which sparsifies refusal steering vectors by 90-99% with little performance loss.

title: Can a small open model notice when it is being steered? Replicating steering-awareness
quick_reasoning: Whether steering leaves a probeable signature undermines invisible-steering assumptions in safety evals, directly relevant.

original_idea.body:

quick_reasoning: Reducing collateral capability damage from safety steering is a directly relevant, scoped deployment question.

original_idea.body:
# Generative causal mediation vs. plain CAA: which gives a cleaner safety steering vector?

**Problem:** A 2026 method, Activation Steering via Generative Causal Mediation, claims cleaner targeting than naive CAA by isolating the causal mediator of a behavior. Whether this reduces the 'feature entanglement' that makes safety steering damage unrelated capabilities is untested in a head-to-head on small models.

**Direction:** For one safety concept (e.g. refusal) on one open model, build steering vectors two ways: standard CAA and the causal-mediation variant. Apply each at matched behavioral effect and measure collateral damage — degradation on unrelated capability benchmarks (e.g. a small MMLU/GSM8K subset). Report which method steers safety with less side-effect.

**Why it matters:** Steering that quietly degrades general capability is a hidden cost that discourages real deployment of safety steering. A clean side-effect comparison tells the open community whether the fancier method is worth it. Inference-only, fits one GPU.

**Relevant context:** Extends 'Activation Steering via Generative Causal Mediation' (arXiv:2602.16080, ~Feb 2026), compared against Contrastive Activation Addition (arXiv:2312.06681).

title: Semantic-cue steering of VLM safety judgments: replicating and red-teaming SAVeS
quick_reasoning: Flipping a VLM safety judge toward false-safe verdicts is a specific, focused content-moderation bypass safety problem.

original_idea.body:
# Semantic-cue steering of VLM safety judgments: replicating and red-teaming SAVeS

**Problem:** SAVeS (2026) steers safety JUDGMENTS in vision-language models via semantic cues. If safety judgments are this steerable, an adversary could also nudge a VLM safety classifier into mislabeling harmful images as safe — the dual-use risk of judgment-steering is unexamined.

**Direction:** On a small open VLM acting as a safety judge over a small image set, replicate cue-based steering of its safety verdicts. Then flip it adversarially: find semantic cues / steering directions that push the judge toward FALSE 'safe' verdicts on genuinely harmful images. Measure how easily the safety judge is flipped and characterize the most effective cues.

**Why it matters:** VLM-based content moderation is widely deployed; if its judgments are cheaply steerable toward 'safe,' that's a concrete bypass of a safety filter. Demonstrating the attack on an open VLM is exactly lab-independent red-teaming, and extends concept steering to multimodal (an open problem).

**Relevant context:** Extends 'SAVeS: Steering Safety Judgments in Vision-Language Models via Semantic Cues' (arXiv:2603.19092, ~Mar 2026).

title: Steering strength as a dial for the safety-vs-coherence frontier
quick_reasoning: Mapping the safety-vs-coherence frontier of steering is a directly relevant, scoped practical-guidance safety study.

original_idea.body:
# Steering strength as a dial for the safety-vs-coherence frontier

**Problem:** Most steering papers report effectiveness at one strength, but excessive steering pushes activations off-manifold and degrades fluency/coherence. The full safety-vs-coherence Pareto frontier per safety concept is rarely mapped, leaving practitioners guessing at a good operating point.

**Direction:** On one open model, sweep steering strength across a fine grid for 3 safety concepts (refusal, anti-toxicity, honesty). At each strength measure (a) the safety behavior gain and (b) a cheap coherence/fluency proxy (perplexity on benign text + a short quality rating). Plot the Pareto frontier per concept and identify the knee point. Compare frontiers across concepts.

**Why it matters:** A reusable 'how hard can I steer before the model breaks' map is immediately practical guidance the open community lacks, and reveals whether some safety concepts are unsteerable without wrecking coherence. Pure inference, one GPU, clean success criteria — ideal first deliverable.

**Relevant context:** Synthesizes the off-manifold/coherence-degradation findings of 'Understanding (Un)Reliability of Steering Vectors' (arXiv:2602.17881, Feb 2026) with steering-strength sensitivity from the safety-pitfalls audit (arXiv:2603.24543, Mar 2026).

title: Replicating the Refusal Direction Across Smaller Open Models
quick_reasoning: Robustness of one-line refusal-ablation jailbreak in tiny misusable open models is a specific, focused safety question.

original_idea.body:
# Replicating the Refusal Direction Across Smaller Open Models

**Problem:** Arditi et al. showed that refusal in LLMs is mediated by a single residual-stream direction across 13 chat models up to 72B. It is unclear how robustly this 'one-dimensional refusal' result holds in the very small instruction-tuned models (Gemma-2-2b-it, Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct) that hobbyists actually run, and whether the direction transfers cleanly between them.

**Direction:** Use TransformerLens to extract the difference-of-means refusal direction (harmful minus harmless prompts) at each layer of three small open chat models. Measure how much ablating the single direction reduces refusal and how much adding it induces refusal on harmless prompts, reproducing the original metrics. The twist: cross-apply each model's direction to the other models (after basis alignment) to test whether the direction is model-universal or idiosyncratic at small scale.

**Why it matters:** Refusal-direction ablation is a one-line jailbreak that requires no lab infrastructure and works on any downloadable open model, so understanding its robustness at the scale defenders cannot control is directly safety-relevant. Establishing whether the single-direction result degrades or stays clean in 1-2B models tells us how brittle open-weight safety tuning is for the models most likely to be misused locally.

**Relevant context:** Arditi et al. 2024 (arXiv:2406.11717) 'Refusal in Language Models Is Mediated by a Single Direction' found a one-dimensional refusal subspace across 13 open chat models up to 72B; ablating it disables refusal with minimal capability loss, adding it induces refusal on harmless prompts. TransformerLens (MIT, 50+ models) supports difference-of-means direction extraction.
